issues.description: The problem statement/UML defines the inventory component as class "Stock" (with methods add/take/findStockIngredient/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock) and states SealSaloon should have a Stock field named stock. However, both template and solution implement this functionality in a class named "Inventory" while leaving Stock.java empty. This naming mismatch makes it unclear to students whether to implement/modify Stock (per statement) or Inventory (per provided code), and following the statement literally will not match the reference design used by SealSaloon/Main.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across statement, template, and solution: either rename Inventory to Stock and update all references (SealSaloon/Main), or update the problem statement/UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock and remove/ignore Stock.java.

issues.description: calculateRemainingOrderNumber() is specified to print "Order number: 0" and then continue up to "Order number: n" where n equals the remaining order number (i.e., the number of remaining orders). In the solution, the loop bound is computed as "remainingOrders = this.orders.length + 1", causing one extra number to be printed compared to the natural interpretation (for orders.length == 0 it prints 0 and 1). This creates an observable output mismatch for tests based on the statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the printed range with the statement by using the remaining order count as the upper bound (typically orders.length), e.g., set remainingOrders = this.orders.length and loop to print 0..remainingOrders inclusive, or clarify in the statement what "remaining order number" means if +1 is intended.
